draft.emotion: energetic and practical, getting things done around the house
notes: Used reflexively ('lavarse') with the definite article (not a possessive) when washing a part of your own body: 'lavarse las manos' (to wash one's hands).
In Spain, 'fregar' is more common than 'lavar' for washing the dishes ('fregar los platos').
Do not confuse with 'limpiar', which means to clean in general, with or without water.

senses.definition: To clean something, or a part of the body, using water and usually soap.
